The *Tatiyapāṭidesanīya* ("Receiving food from a designated family") is the third rule in the Pāṭidesanīya section of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who accepts food from any family or person designated as "in training" (*sekha*) must formally acknowledge the offense [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text within the Vinaya Piṭaka has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. No relevant secondary literature discussions were present in the retrieved reference literature, where keyword matches were false positives from game-theory literature.

SuttaCentral records full parallels across all major extant Vinaya traditions, including the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-pd3*) and Parivāra (Pāṭidesanīya 3), as well as corresponding rules in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka Vinayas preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit [SuttaCentral].
